description: Flatpay was launched in Copenhagen in 2022, and has since expanded successfully from Denmark to Finland, Germany, Italy, France, and the UK – which is proving its fastest-growing market yet. The company has grown at considerable speed, building a large and loyal merchant base across Europe and achieving over EUR100 million in annual recurring revenue. In November 2025, Flatpay raised EUR145 million, valuing the company at €1.5 billion - becoming Denmark’s fastest-ever unicorn. Dawn first led Flatpay’s €45 million Series B in April 2024, and has continued to reinvest in the company at each subsequent stage. Flatpay has been so successful in part because it has created and scaled a winning combination of customer-centric product, ‘old-school people-led sales’, and state-of-the-art technology. The Flatpay team has built a product that its customers – small merchants – really need. A payments terminal with flat rates and no hidden charges – and they’ve made it accessible and easy-to-use. Their offering is ideal for all the cafes, salons, pizza joints, antique shops and more that sit at the heart of communities across Europe.
tagline: Transparent, affordable payments for small and mid-sized merchants

description: Dataiku is the Platform for AI Success, the enterprise orchestration layer for building, deploying, and governing AI. In a single environment, teams design and operate AI agents, analytics, and machine learning with the transparency, collaboration, and control enterprises require. For more than a decade, Dataiku has helped organizations turn data, analytics, and AI into measurable business value. As the market has evolved from analytics to machine learning to generative AI and agents, Dataiku has enabled customers to stay ahead—operationalizing new technologies while maintaining stability, governance, and trust. Sitting above data platforms, cloud infrastructure, and AI services, Dataiku connects the full enterprise AI stack, enabling organizations to run AI across multi-vendor environments with centralized governance and oversight, at scale.
tagline: The platform for AI success. Powered by people, orchestration, and governance. Built for enterprise scale.

description: Angus and Chris founded Cover Genius to create a scalable platform for embedded insurance distribution that would deliver superior outcomes for insurers, merchants and their end customers. Today, Cover Genius is enabling the world's largest digital platforms to offer personalised insurance and protection products to their customers, programmatically in real-time, all around the world. The model has proven exceptionally scalable. Today, they are powering solutions across verticals from retail, to travel, logistics, mobility and financial services with partners from Booking Holdings to Amazon in more than 60 countries and support millions of consumers.
tagline: The insurance engine for tomorrow’s internet

description: When diffusion models exploded, Flaviu and Ioana couldn’t believe how slow and expensive it was to generate images and video at scale. So, in 2023, they launched a side project with a simple but audacious ambition: to make generating an image as fast as finding one, and affordable for mass use. The project spread by word of mouth as builders discovered a product that was not just faster, but dramatically cheaper than anything else, and therefore scalable to millions of workloads. Demand for an API arrived almost overnight, and the project became Runware: a vertically integrated media-inference platform that makes image, video and audio generation a scalable sub-second process via a single API. Runware’s entire setup and success to date is a reflection of its founders. Flaviu and Ioana are relentless systems thinkers who know where performance actually comes from, and they move fast without breaking the things that matter. They have built the rare platform that delights developers, satisfies enterprise checklists, and bends the cost curve in the customer’s favour. This is a huge, urgent market, and Runware has the right product at the right layer, built by the right team.
tagline: Lowest cost API for image, video and audio generation. Fast, flexible, on demand. Instant scale.

description: By his mid-twenties, Vish had become the youngest-ever Executive Director at EY, spending over a decade building global anti-financial crime programmes for the world's largest banks. The experience gave him a front-row seat to a persistent problem: enterprises sat on billions of data points but could not connect them to make trusted decisions. In 2016, he resigned to build Quantexa and close that gap. Quantexa's contextual decision intelligence platform uses AI to connect siloed and fragmented data, creating a unified, real-world view that reveals hidden relationships, risks and opportunities. The company serves 7 of the top 10 UK and Australian banks, major insurers, telecoms and government agencies worldwide. Dawn invested early and has supported the company through its rapid international expansion via both its flagship and opportunities funds. Quantexa achieved unicorn status with its $153 million Series D in 2022. With over 900 employees across 14 global offices, it is one of the UK's most significant enterprise software companies.
tagline: Creating a new generation of decision intelligence built on context.

description: When Denis Prochko, Blackwall’s CTO, launched a vegetarian recipe site as a passion project, he had no idea it would lead to the founding of one of the most remarkable infrastructure companies on the market. The site’s rapid success attracted more than just food enthusiasts, it also became a target for relentless bot traffic. While some bots were harmless, others attempted to steal intellectual property, commit ad fraud, or exploit vulnerabilities. Together, this bot traffic overwhelmed the ‘good’ traffic the business relied upon. Then came Blackwall – a game-changing solution in bot mitigation. Today, Blackwall primarily serves Hosting Service Providers (HSPs) while also offering its product to Managed Service Providers (MSPs), both of which protect thousands of small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). Powered by AI, Blackwall delivers a 30% improvement in malicious activity detection while cutting aftercare costs by 15-20%, making security more efficient and cost-effective for its partners. Blackwall was founded by Nik Rozenberg and Denis Prochko in 2019 and is headquartered in Tallinn, Estonia.
tagline: High-performance web security & traffic filtering for hosting providers

description: Daniel and Fredrik were early pioneers in their vision to create a more open financial system in Europe. Long-term friends and repeat entrepreneurs, they founded Tink in Stockholm in 2012 to build data-driven and personalised financial products for Europe consumers. Seeing the disruptive potential of emerging open banking regulations in 2018, and the opportunity to take a strategic position in the ecosystem, Tink pivoted into a B2B infrastructure platform, built standardized API connectivity to thousands of European banks - the rails and brains of open banking data - and quickly assumed market leadership. We led Tink's €90 million Series D in 2020 and co-led the €85 million Series E later that year. In June 2021, the company was acquired by Visa $2.2 billion, a testament to the determination, vision and hard work of the whole Tink team. Tink's founders Daniel Kjellen and Fredrik Hedberg
tagline: Laying the foundations for open banking in Europe

description: In founding iZettle, Jacob and Magnus revolutionised mobile payments with the world’s first mini-chip card reader and software for mobile devices – helping small businesses succeed in a world of giants. Bought (and renamed Zettle) by PayPal for $2.2bn in 2018 to form the company’s point of sale solution, the team is continuing its original mission: giving small businesses in Europe and Latin America the tools to get paid, track sales and grow.
tagline: Helping small businesses succeed with mobile payments.

description: Peter Bauer and Neil Murray, two South African expatriates based in London, founded Mimecast in 2003 after recognising the growing vulnerabilities in corporate email as businesses became ever more dependent on digital communications. Peter had cut his teeth as a Microsoft systems engineer in the mid-1990s before moving to the UK, where he and Neil set about building a cloud-based platform to protect, manage, and archive email for enterprises. From its London base, Mimecast grew into one of the world's leading email security companies, expanding aggressively into North America and listing on NASDAQ in November 2015. Dawn was an early and important institutional investor, supporting the company through a period of transformational growth during which Mimecast went from under $10m of revenue to a global cybersecurity leader.
tagline: Making email security simple for every business

description: Felix Van de Maele, Stijn Christiaens, and Pieter De Leenheer were classmates and researchers at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel when they recognised that enterprises were collecting vast pools of data but had no systematic way to understand, trust, or govern it. In 2008, amid the global financial crisis, they founded Collibra in Brussels to bring order to the chaos with a collaborative data governance platform. The early years were about survival and product development, but the company's breakthrough came as regulation (GDPR, CCPA) and the explosion of enterprise data created urgent demand for data intelligence. Collibra expanded to New York, built a blue-chip customer base including major financial institutions and Fortune 500 companies, and raised over $590 million in venture funding. Dawn first invested at the Series B stage and has participated in every subsequent round through to the company's Series G in 2021, which valued Collibra at $5.25 billion. Today, with over 700 customers worldwide, Collibra is the category-defining leader in data intelligence.
tagline: The data intelligence platform aligning every person, team and system with trusted data

description: The enterprise tech stack of the future is fragmented, flexible and well-governed, making software stack management vital. André and the LeanIX team spearheaded this trend. With over 1,000 other leading global brands, such as Atlassian, Volkswagen and Adidas, among its customers, LeanIX’s continuous transformation platform enables enterprises to make faster, data-driven decisions about their IT infrastructure. Businesses get a real-time overview of all the software they use, including how it all fits together, which teams are using it and how it can be put to better use, to improve productivity and accelerate transformation. In September 2023, LeanIX was acquired by SAP. LeanIX had been a strategic partner of SAP for over a decade and complements SAP’s transformation capabilities, providing its customers with access to the full suite of tools required for continuous business transformation and AI-enabled process optimisation. The acquisition reflects the powerful impact of LeanIX’s product suite and partnerships, and is testament to the exceptional discipline and focus with which Andre and the LeanIX team have executed since they founded the business.
tagline: Enterprise architecture and SaaS management to shape and control a complex IT landscape.

description: Fonoa enables fast-moving, high-volume online businesses to automate all aspects of tax, from determining and calculating which taxes apply to transactions to generating locally compliant invoices and reporting to relevant authorities. By removing one of the biggest roadblocks for international scaling and expansion – managing complex tax issues across multiple geographies and jurisdictions – Fonoa helps businesses to sell anything, anywhere while remaining fully compliant, scalable and efficient. Building on their own experience expanding Uber’s European business, founders Davor and the team have attracted some of the biggest names in marketplaces and digital content, making taxes simple, automated and borderless, and helping their customers grow at the speed of their ambition.
tagline: Tax infrastructure that connects the full indirect tax lifecycle on one platform

description: Matthew O'Riordan and Paddy Byers founded Ably in London in 2016 to build a platform that removes the complexity of real-time infrastructure. Ably helps teams deliver resilient AI UX and high-performance live experiences that stay fast and in sync worldwide, providing the global realtime layer for AI agents, chat, notifications, live dashboards, and collaboration - engineered to handle peak demand without self-managed infrastructure. Teams like HubSpot and Intercom use Ably to avoid the cost and complexity of building and operating realtime systems, while still getting predictable performance at serious scale, serving 2B+ devices and handling 2T+ API operations per month. Ably's Pub/Sub, Chat, and AI Transport products are unified by design, with developer-friendly APIs and SDKs that integrate across the stack.
tagline: The global realtime layer for AI agents, chat, notifications, live dashboards, and collaboration

description: Creating a cloud ecosystem for data and workflow management Fintech veterans Roy and Steve founded AccessFintech to solve a data distribution challenge: how to get capital market participants out of silos and to share trade data more efficiently. AccessFintech’s platform provides a scalable self-service infrastructure for sharing, governing and working with trade data in the cloud. It is enabling buyside and sellside institutions to collaborate, standardise workflows and drive significant operational and capital efficiencies through their middle and back offices. The largest financial institutions from Goldman Sachs, to JP Morgan and Bank of New York are partnering with AccessFintech and joining this data network - Synergy - to join their clients and counterparties in a complete ecosystem for data and workflow management.
tagline: Evolving the financial industry operating model through a collaborative data network.

description: Matthias and Christian founded Billie to reimagine the way that businesses would pay on terms as B2B commerce moves online. Their platform enables merchant partners to offer seamless payment terms and finance to business customers at checkout, and benefit from full credit and fraud risk protection. Operating at the intersection of fintech and B2B commerce, Billie addresses a massive market: trade credit is one of the largest sources of short-term business financing in Europe. By automating the entire process from real-time credit scoring to payment collection, Billie drives higher conversion rates and larger basket sizes for merchants, and offers buyers more flexible and efficient payment solutions.
tagline: Instant financing for B2B merchants in every commerce channel

description: Bondaval’s technology and insurance products are delivering superior credit management and protection for the world’s largest global enterprises. After a successful career in professional sport captaining England’s rugby sevens team, Tom Powell embarked on a career in insurance where he met his co-founder, Sam Damoussi. Together they saw an opportunity to bring something new to a highly-profitable credit insurance industry that had done little to improve products and claims experiences for its enterprise customers. Bondavla’s granular approach to insights, policy design and workflow automation are a step-change for enterprises to effectively optimize and automate risk management in their supply chain and accounts receivable - protecting their business, their bottom line and improving capital efficiency.
tagline: Credit risk OS

description: Lena saw an opportunity to bring real-time account-to-account payments to Europe’s merchants and consumers - secure and seamless payments, instantly settled. Following leadership roles at Klarna and as CEO of Qliro, Lena founded Brite Payments in Stockholm in 2019. Today, Brite’s instant payments network processes real-time bank payments and payouts all across Europe. Consumers authenticate using their bank's existing identification method, with no sign-up or card details required. The result is a complete end-to-end instant payments solution: pay-ins, payouts, collection accounts, and multi-currency settlement provided through a single integration.
tagline: Secure and instant bank payments for merchants and consumers

description: Michael Grupp, Micha-Manuel Bues and Michael Huebl founded BRYTER in Berlin to democratise automation in knowledge-intensive industries. The team had backgrounds in professional services and saw that lawyers, compliance officers, and consultants spent enormous amounts of time on repetitive, rules-based work that could be automated without writing a single line of code. BRYTER has become the legal platform that provides end-to-end automation combining AI with workflows, offering a full AI productivity suite for lawyers comprising: BEAMON AI: actionable AI tools that help lawyers research, draft and review contracts; and BRYTER Workflows the no-code platform for legal engineers to use rule-based and AI workflows to automate legal processes.
tagline: Make AI work for legal

description: Copper was founded by Dmitry Tokarev in 2018 to provide institutional-grade infrastructure for the digital assets market. The platform supports custody, prime brokerage, collateral management and post trade services for financial institutions and trading firms. This includes the market’s largest global off-exchange settlement network allowing institutions to eliminate exchange counterparty risk. The company has offices across London, New York, Singapore, Abu Dhabi, and Zug and is licensed internationally. In October 2024, Copper appointed Amar Kuchinad as Global CEO to lead the company’s next phase of growth. With experiences leading capital markets technology scale-ups and executive roles at Goldman Sachs and the SEC, Amar brings deep capital markets and regulatory experience.
tagline: Institutional custody, prime services and collateral management for digital assets

description: Audit firms are under growing pressure to deliver higher-quality work with more data, higher standards, fewer auditors and less margin for error. Many firms have started experimenting with general AI, but audit requires a higher standard. Every result needs to be explainable, reviewable and defensible. Cortea is built for that environment: AI agents purpose-built for audit quality, with auditors always in control of judgement and final sign-off. Cortea’s Audit Quality Agents support the completion stage of the audit, where final review happens before an audit report goes out. Cortea works with innovative audit firms across Europe, the UK, and the US. We backed Cortea in their seed round, alongside heavyweight industry executives including Larry Bradley, former Senior Partner and Global Head of Audit for KPMG, Simon Collins, former Senior Partner and UK Chairman of KPMG and Davor Tremac, founder and CEO of Fonoa.
tagline: Agentic OS for audit services

description: Erik Lien, Anders Frostad and Tobias Gundhus founded C Two (originally RPA Supervisor) in Bergen, Norway, in 2018 after seeing the same problem play out across large enterprises: businesses were investing heavily in robotic process automation, but the tools they bought to automate tasks could not themselves be managed at scale. As companies deployed hundreds of software robots across departments and systems, they had no way to orchestrate them, monitor performance against SLAs, or diagnose failures without throwing people at the problem. The promise of automation was being undermined by the operational burden of running it. That challenge has only intensified as enterprises now deploy AI agents alongside RPA bots, APIs and human handoffs, creating new layers of complexity and unpredictability. C Two's agentic management platform provides a single operating layer that unifies all of these technologies, giving enterprises universal orchestration, governance and real-time intelligence across their entire automation estate. The platform dynamically reroutes work to the best available resource based on real-time performance, cost and SLA pressure, and automatically resolves 90 per cent of L0 and L1 failures without human intervention. Critically, C Two works across vendors, meaning organisations are not locked into any single provider. The company now serves over 200 enterprises and has been recognised by HFS Research as a Hot Vendor. In February 2026, C Two appointed Paul Donaldson as CEO and Colin Redbond as Chief Product and Technology Officer as the company scales its next phase of growth.
tagline: The agentic era automation operating system, orchestrating agents, bots, APIs and people across business processes

description: Customer feedback is a vital source of insight, yet unlocking its value has traditionally been manual and fragmented. What if an AI platform could collect, analyse, and act on customer feedback at scale, with human-level accuracy? Former Google engineers Nima Vali Rajabi and Francisco Arias have built deepdots, an end-to-end solution for streamlining customer feedback analysis. Customer experience and product teams no longer have to waste time searching through disparate silos for data, or spend hours manually sifting through feedback, as deepdots integrates collection, analysis and action in a single platform. The platform also dramatically improves feedback quality while enabling customers to be more specific, all without compromising privacy or safety, thanks to its proprietary in-house models. Since launching in 2023, deepdots has attracted large enterprises as customers in its home market, including pharmacy chain Matas (263 stores, 4BN kroner+), real estate firm NREP, and water solutions leader Culligan.
tagline: AI feedback intelligence

description: Meryem Arik, Dr Jamie Dborin, and Dr Fergus Finn founded Doubleword (originally TitanML) in London in 2021 to solve one of the biggest barriers to enterprise AI adoption: self-hosted inference. During their postdoctoral research at UCL, Jamie and Fergus discovered that techniques from their quantum machine learning work could dramatically improve AI inference performance. Together with Meryem, who studied theoretical physics and philosophy at Oxford, they set out to make self-hosting AI models as straightforward as using third-party APIs. Inference is where AI delivers real-world value, transforming trained models into business outcomes. As enterprises increasingly need to own and control this capability for reasons of cost, security, and performance, the challenge of building and maintaining the underlying infrastructure has become a major bottleneck. Doubleword's platform enables one-click deployment of any open-source, proprietary, or fine-tuned model across cloud and on-premise environments, with built-in monitoring, logging, and GPU resource management. The company has already secured partnerships with Snowflake, Dataiku, and Nvidia, and counts major enterprises in pharma, manufacturing, and finance among its customers. We led Doubleword's $12 million Series A in May 2025. The company is one of the earliest movers in the inference space, having been founded before ChatGPT brought large language models into the mainstream. Doubleword is now expanding its team globally and deepening its platform capabilities as enterprise demand for self-hosted AI accelerates.
tagline: Enabling self-hosted AI inference

description: Lewis and the Eigen team helped businesses unlock the value of their documents and data, and turn them into a strategic asset – extracting the answers they need for faster, smarter decisions.
tagline: Powering enterprise automation with AI.

description: Elwood provides front-to-back institutional-grade infrastructure for leading trading firms facing the digital asset markets. The platform aggregates access to liquidity venues and allows institutions to manage the full lifecycle of their trading activities through execution, portfolio management, risk and collateral workflows - helping clients trade with greater efficiency, control and transparency.
tagline: Supporting institutional trading and risk management in the digital assets market

description: Firebolt's architecture was designed from the ground up for speed and efficiency, delivering sub-second query performance on massive datasets at a fraction of the cost of incumbent solutions. Traditional warehouses and lakehouses force you to choose between performance, cost, and simplicity. Firebolt delivers all three on a single platform—with the best price-performance in the market so you can ship faster without compromises. Firebolt is built for companies that need their data platforms to do more — run AI workloads, power sub-second customer-facing analytics at scale, or execute ELT jobs efficiently at a fraction of the cost.
tagline: AI agents, sub-second analytics and efficient ELT with the best price-performance in the market

description: FlowX.AI is an AI-native agent platform built to make enterprise AI production-grade in mission-critical, highly regulated environments. With 140+ ready-made agents and plug-in integration into the systems you already have, FlowX.AI helps clients move beyond pilots and go live in as fast as 4 weeks, without development cycles, while maintaining built-in governance, compliance controls, auditability, and strict security and data privacy. The result is faster, more reliable decisions and automation across core workflows like onboarding, lending, underwriting, claims, and logistics operations, delivering measurable efficiency gains and strong ROI without compromising control or compliance. FlowX.AI is trusted by leading institutions, including State Street, OTP Group, Banca Transilvania, and Triglav, and is designed for mission-critical performance with 99.99% robustness and enterprise-grade security.
tagline: Deploy banking, insurance, and logistics AI Agents in weeks

description: David Garfield and Henry Harrison founded Garrison in London in 2014 to build hardware-enforced web isolation technology. The pair had worked together at national security specialist Detica and subsequently established the cyber security business unit at BAE Systems, giving them deep domain expertise in protecting the most sensitive government environments. They recognised that organisations faced an impossible trade-off: restrict web access and cripple productivity, or allow open browsing and accept the risk of web-borne threats like phishing, ransomware and drive-by downloads. Garrison's answer was a radically different approach the company called "hardsec". Rather than relying on software virtualisation, Garrison engineered a dedicated hardware platform using ARM processor chips that turned web content into compressed, encrypted video streams, physically isolating browsing activity from the corporate network. The technology was independently verified to levels that earned the trust of highly sensitive government organisations, while remaining practical and affordable enough for commercial enterprises. Garrison’s customers included the UK Government, the US Federal Government and major commercial institutions such as Lloyds Banking Group, spanning the banking, insurance, media, telecoms and legal sectors. Dawn led the company's $30 million Series B in 2018. In June 2024, Garrison was acquired by Everfox, the TPG-backed high-assurance cybersecurity platform, combining Garrison's hardsec browser isolation and cross-domain solutions with Everfox's existing portfolio to create a broader defence-grade security offering.
tagline: Ultra-secure web isolation

description: Henrik Muller-Hansen founded Gelato in Oslo with a vision to localise global print production. His insight was that the print industry was fundamentally inefficient: orders shipped long distances, generating waste, cost, and carbon emissions, when the same products could be printed on demand at facilities closer to the end customer. Gelato built a platform connecting creators and e-commerce businesses with a network of over 100 print partners in 32 countries. Whether a customer orders a t-shirt in Tokyo or a canvas print in Toronto, Gelato routes the job to the nearest production facility, cutting delivery times, costs, and environmental impact. The platform now serves millions of creators and businesses worldwide.
tagline: The world's largest platform for on-demand, localised print production

description: Asaf Ezra and Tal Saiag founded Granulate in Tel Aviv in 2018 to tackle one of the cloud era's most pressing cost problems: the waste of compute resources. Their AI-powered software agent could be installed on any workload in minutes and, without requiring a single line of code change, would learn an application's behaviour and continuously optimise its resource usage, cutting cloud costs by up to 60 per cent. Granulate's relationship with Intel began in 2019, when the company was part of the first graduating class of Intel Ignite, the chipmaker's start-up accelerator. The two companies went on to collaborate closely, optimising workload performance for customers running on Intel processors. We participated in Granulate's $30 million Series B in 2021, when the company was just two years old. Less than a year later, in March 2022, Intel acquired Granulate for approximately $650 million.
tagline: Cutting costs and improving performance with real-time continuous optimisation.

description: Harbr is creating a new paradigm: a future where every enterprise can turn their datasets into saleable assets. Gary, Anthony and the Harbr team have built the enterprise data exchange platform that enables companies to productise and securely share their data, both internally and with other organisations – increasing access, insights and collaboration, all while maintaining control and governance.
tagline: The platform powering the world’s best data marketplaces and storefronts

description: Mika Aalto, Pyry Åvist, Karri Kurunmäki and Pasi Salo founded Hoxhunt in Helsinki in 2016 out of frustration with the state of corporate security awareness training. Traditional programmes treated cybersecurity education as a compliance exercise: employees sat through annual slide decks, ticked a box and forgot everything by the following week. Meanwhile, phishing remained the primary entry point for the vast majority of corporate cyber incidents. The founders saw that the problem was not a lack of awareness but a lack of genuine behaviour change. Hoxhunt built a human risk management platform that goes beyond awareness to measurably reduce cyber risk. The platform combines AI and behavioural science to deliver personalised, gamified micro-training that adapts to each employee's skill level. Realistic phishing simulations are sent continuously, and when employees spot and report them, they earn points and climb leaderboards, turning what was previously a tedious obligation into something people actively engage with. Critically, Hoxhunt also automates incident remediation, helping security operations teams respond faster with fewer resources, while giving security leaders outcome-driven metrics to demonstrate reduced risk. Hoxhunt works with major global enterprises and has won numerous industry awards.Dawn led Hoxhunt's Series A in 2018, alongside Icebreaker.vc and Risto Siilasmaa, the former chairman of Nokia. The company went on to raise a $40 million Series B led by Level Equity in 2022.
tagline: Personalised security awareness & phishing training experiences that employees love

description: inforcer has a unique value proposition as the cornerstone between one of the world’s largest companies, Microsoft, and MSPs that serve as trusted advisors on billions of dollars in IT spend. inforcer is the key to unlocking AI and security adoption across SMBs globally - SMBs that form the backbone of many economies Microsoft has become a leader in productivity, cloud computing, security, and AI. Its best-in-class unified offering makes it a vendor of choice for 80% of SMBs, spanning 350 million users globally. Without in-house resources or the expertise to source, implement, and maintain IT products, including the Microsoft suite, SMBs look to MSPs to help them navigate their choices. This means securing and productising Microsoft 365 environments is no longer optional for MSPs. But it takes time, significant manual effort and a highly specialist skillset to achieve this at scale, leaving many MSPs unable to leverage the Microsoft platform fully. Using inforcer solves these challenges seamlessly for all stakeholders, unlocking the business case for MSPs to service the Microsoft security and AI technology stack. inforcer’s cloud-first, end-to-end and collaborative product allows MSPs to easily standardise, roll out, back up, restore and manage Microsoft 365 policies across multiple Microsoft tenants, regardless of their size and complexity. Built and funded by MSP veterans and the community, inforcer helps MSPs become and remain compliant, and develop into security and AI experts, staying at the edge of the latest technology innovations. And as AI adoption accelerates, with inforcer, MSPs can focus on what is most important: cementing trust with their end customers and, ultimately, serving them better. Since launching in 2022, inforcer has been adopted by high-profile MSPs and groups across the US, EMEA and APAC, and become an essential tool in the modern, cloud-first, MSP software stack.
tagline: The Microsoft 365 multi-tenant management platform for MSPs

description: Kraaft is a communication platform designed for construction professionals, streamlining project management by centralising photos, voice notes, and documents into dedicated project conversations. Each project has its own conversation thread, allowing team members to share time-stamped and geotagged photos, messages, and plans, enhancing collaboration between field and office teams. The platform offers features such as custom reports and alerts, enabling users to generate reports for change orders or internal tracking. Kraaft integrates with tools like SharePoint, Google Drive, Word, QuickBooks, B2W, and HCSS, ensuring seamless connectivity with existing systems. With over 230,000 construction projects managed, Kraaft has earned the trust of more than 950 clients. The platform is recognised for its simplicity and effectiveness, making it a preferred choice among construction site managers. Kraaft was founded by Marc Nègre (CPO), Cédric Boidin (CTO) and Thomas Reygagne (CEO) in Paris in 2020. The team is now planning expansion of its services into the UK and Germany.
tagline: The mobile-first platform for construction professionals

description: Salespeople by trade and nature, Olli and Lauri started LeadDesk to revolutionise the call centre industry, to help every sales and customer service agent close more deals and resolve more cases. Fully customisable campaigns, queues, reports and operations – LeadDesk’s software replaces inefficient, fragmented legacy solutions and gives people the tools to have better conversations. It’s used by over 20,000 agents across more than 30 countries on a daily basis, helping to close more than 100,000 – and counting – deals per week. LeadDesk went public in 2019, listing on Nasdaq First North.
tagline: Cloud-based contact centre software for European businesses

description: Petr Antropov and Nick Ustinov founded Lokalise in Riga, Latvia, in 2017 after running into the localisation problem first-hand. While building a mobile app that grew past a million users across multiple language markets, they found that existing translation management tools were slow, lacked context, and required tedious manual work. Ustinov, a self-taught developer, built a custom tool to automate translation and maintain context within the app. It proved to be a product with demand well beyond their own needs. Lokalise has since evolved beyond a traditional translation management system into a full localization platform combining AI orchestration, human translation, and workflow automation. The platform automatically selects between multiple AI engines based on context, language pair and content type, while integrating with over 60 tools including GitHub, GitLab, Figma, Contentful and Zendesk. Teams across product, engineering, design, marketing and localisation use it to translate apps, websites, games and marketing content with continuous localisation baked into their existing workflows. The company now serves over 3,000 organisations worldwide, including Mastercard, Toyota, HP, Revolut, Notion and Yelp
tagline: The localization platform helping 3,000+ companies go global in every language

description: Asaf Peled and Gilad Bechar founded Minute Media in Tel Aviv in 2011 to build the next generation of sports and entertainment media. The company operates a portfolio of premium digital brands, including The Players' Tribune, FanSided, and 90min, alongside a proprietary publishing platform that powers content creation and distribution at scale. Minute Media has grown into a global media business reaching hundreds of millions of fans each month. The company achieved unicorn status in 2024. Dawn has been a long-standing investor, first backing the company in 2015 and supporting its growth over nearly a decade.
tagline: The next generation of sports and entertainment media

description: Founded in 2022, Oneleet is the all-in-one security compliance platform that ends the “compliance theater” that leaves companies vulnerable to attacks and delivers real security. Co-founder and CEO Bryan Onel spent years simulating advanced attacks and modeling defensive solutions for hundreds of companies as a penetration tester and vulnerability assessor. He realised that compliance had become a checkbox exercise which did not protect companies, which were relying on existing “AI automation” platforms that were not truly securing their businesses – or on slow and expensive manual processes. Oneleet is unique in the space thanks to its platform that tightly couples compliance and security, providing a seamless experience for customers and superior outcomes.
tagline: Real security, not just compliance theatre

description: Hugo and Paul founded Omi to build the foundational infrastructure for brands to scale visual content production. With Omi’s 3D twins, every AI-generated visual asset is grounded in a brand’s product truth - validated, governed, and production-ready. This ensures no hallucinations, no brand risk, and no compliance exposure. Omi empowers marketing teams to scale on-brand and compliant visual content at AI speed with consistency across every channel, whilst cutting the cost of production by up to 90%. The platform is trusted by leading brand groups such as LVMH, L’Oréal, Estee Lauder and Nestlé across the US and Europe.
tagline: 3D twins powering AI visual production workflows and brand governance at scale

description: Pedro Castillo is a rare breed of repeat founder. As the creator, CEO, and CTO of Devo, the cloud analytics and security platform valued at over $2 billion, he had spent years on the receiving end of the enterprise data deluge. He saw first-hand how his customers struggled to understand what data was where, what value it had, and where it went. He searched for a solution and found nothing that cut through. So he decided to build one himself. Pedro and his co-founders, Lucas Varela and Pedro Tortosa, launched Onum in Madrid in late 2023. Their observability pipeline platform allows companies to tune out the noise in their data, isolating what is genuinely business-critical from the rest. Cstomers saw data management costs fall by up to 80 per cent within days of implementation. We led Onum's $28 million Series A in April 2024. In August 2025, less than two years after launching, Onum was acquired by CrowdStrike, in a standout validation of the product, the team, and the urgency of the problem they solved.
tagline: Less noise. More value. Real-time data intelligence.

description: OpenGamma’s platform provides the foundation for a new treasury paradigm in capital markets. Sophisticated analytics and workflow automations help firms to optimize their margin requirements and collateral management strategies across derivatives positions, manage their liquidity risk, and dramatically improve capital efficiency. Trusted by the world’s most sophisticated hedge funds, commodities firms, global investment banks and asset managers, OpenGamma is helping firms turn treasury management into a competitive advantage. OpenGamma was acquired by Trading Technologies in December 2025.
tagline: Reinventing treasury management for financial markets firms

description: 80% of the world’s workforce operates on the frontlines of essential industries: the 2.7 billion healthcare workers, retail associates, warehouse operators, hospitality staff and logistics drivers who keep economies running. The difference between a staffed shift and an unstaffed one directly impacts revenue, customer experience and operational performance. Yet most enterprise software built over the past two decades was designed for desk-based knowledge workers. Frontline employees are often deskless, without corporate email addresses, and are reached through messaging and phone calls rather than software logins. As a result, frontline hiring and workforce management still relies heavily on fragmented manual processes, spreadsheets and large operational teams, consuming significant time and costing organisations billions every year. The cost is felt on both sides. Annual employee turnover exceeds 70% in many frontline sectors, leaving recruiters and operations teams buried in administrative work while unfilled roles create operational drag. At the same time, workers often enter jobs without proper onboarding, lose contact with employers within days, and leave within weeks. Orbio is building an AI workforce platform designed for frontline industries. Its agents can conduct interviews, assess candidate fit and motivation, guide new hires through onboarding, monitor engagement and churn signals, and remain in contact with employees throughout their lifecycle — from first application through to tenure and exit. For employers, this creates a fundamentally new operating model: the ability to engage and support frontline workforces 24/7 while delegating large parts of workforce operations to AI agents. The result is faster hiring, lower administrative burden, improved retention and a more resilient operational workforce. Orbio already works with global enterprise customers including Poke House, YUM! Brands (which owns brands including KFC, Taco Bell and Pizza Hut), and AWWG (the global fashion group operating Hackett, Pepe Jeans and Tommy Hilfiger licenses). These companies use Orbio’s AI agents to hire, onboard, manage and retain frontline employees at scale. Operating autonomously across channels including messaging and phone calls, Orbio’s agents can engage candidates and employees directly, handling hiring, onboarding, engagement and offboarding workflows for both full-time and shift-based workforces. Orbio’s expansion is backed by audited results across Orbio's current markets: over 60% time-to-hire reduction at a pan-European security customer, 60% productivity gains at Poke House, and 70% recruiter productivity uplift across multi-language retail in Benelux.
tagline: Orbio helps global enterprises automate frontline hiring, onboarding and workforce management with its team of AI agents

description: Emil Eifrem sketched the idea for what would become the property graph model on the back of a napkin during a flight to Mumbai in 2000. Together with co-founder Johan Svensson, he spent the next decade building Neo4j from a garage project in Malmo, Sweden, into the world's leading graph database. Their founding conviction was that data's real value lies not in individual records, but in the connections between them. In 2010, Neo4j launched as an open-source graph database and quickly attracted a global community of developers alongside enterprise customers spanning financial services, logistics, healthcare, and technology. Trusted by organisations from NASA to Airbnb, the platform powers fraud detection, real-time recommendations, and supply chain analysis for some of the world's most data-intensive businesses. Dawn participated in Neo4j's $20 million Series C in 2015. The company went on to reach a valuation north of $2 billion and is now listed on Nasdaq North.
tagline: The graph database powering meaningful insights and intelligent applications.

description: Qogita is a leading global wholesale B2B platform that offers a wide variety of products, brands and categories across geographies. The company caters to a large range of organizations, from small retailers to large brands. With Qogita, customers generate higher margins and greater turnover whilst reducing labor cost by using our technology infrastructure. In short: Qogita simplifies business-to-business trade.
tagline: Bringing transparency and efficiency to wholesale procurement

description: Peter Aschmoneit founded Quantilope in Hamburg to automate consumer insights. Traditional market research was slow, expensive, and dependent on armies of analysts. Quantilope built a platform that automates the entire insights process, from survey design to advanced analytics, delivering results in hours rather than weeks. Quantilope serves major global brands across consumer goods, retail, and media. Dawn invested to support the company's growth and international expansion.
tagline: Automating consumer insights from survey to analysis

description: Anurag Gupta, a former Vice President of Amazon Aurora at AWS, co-founded Shoreline in Redwood City in 2019 to bring real-time automation to cloud operations. Having spent eight years building cloud infrastructure at Amazon-scale, Anurag understood that operations teams were drowning in manual incident response, fixing the same known issues repeatedly when those fixes could and should be automated. Shoreline's platform made it easy for operators to create automated remediations for well-known issues and scale them instantly across entire cloud fleets. In June 2024, Shoreline was acquired by Nvidia for approximately $100 million, as the chipmaker continued to build out its software capabilities for data centre and cloud customers. Dawn participated in the company's Series B.
tagline: Cloud operations optimisation

description: Pieterjan Bouten and Louis Jonckheere founded Showpad in Ghent, Belgium, in 2011 to bridge the gap between marketing and sales. Their insight was that sales teams were struggling to find, personalise, and deliver the right content at the right moment in the buyer's journey, and marketing teams had no visibility into what happened after content was created. Showpad's sales enablement platform became a category leader, trusted by enterprise sales organisations across the globe to train reps, manage content, and coach teams through data-driven insights. The company expanded from Belgium into the US and across Europe, building a substantial recurring revenue base. Showpad was acquired by Vector Capital in 2025, validating the strength of the platform and the sales enablement category that Pieterjan and Louis helped to define.
tagline: Keeping marketing and sales in sync to drive more sales.

description: Carlo Gualandri founded Soldo in London to give businesses complete control over their spending. Having previously built Gioco Digitale, one of Italy's most successful online gaming companies, Carlo turned his attention to corporate expense management, where employees and finance teams alike were trapped in a cycle of lost receipts, manual reconciliation, and delayed reporting. Soldo's spend management platform combines smart company cards with real-time tracking, automated expense reporting, and granular spending controls. The product resonated immediately with mid-market and enterprise businesses across Europe, and the company has grown to serve tens of thousands of organisations.
tagline: Complete control over company spending, from petty cash to procurement

description: Christian Lund and Jesper Theill Eriksen founded Templafy in Copenhagen to solve a problem hiding in plain sight inside every large organisation: the chaos of business content creation. Every day, employees across the enterprise generate millions of documents, presentations, and emails, often from outdated templates, with incorrect branding, and without proper compliance safeguards. Templafy's content enablement platform integrates directly into the tools people already use, from Microsoft Office to Google Workspace, ensuring that every piece of content created across the organisation is on-brand, compliant, and based on the latest templates and assets. The company has grown to serve hundreds of enterprise customers globally. Dawn invested to support Templafy's continued growth and international expansion.
tagline: Enabling businesses to create on-brand, high-performing content faster.
